## Audited negative answer; claimed_solved, 2/5
The source-defined normalized equator transform has no uniform reverse Wasserstein bound on all probabilities: antipodal Dirac masses have identical data and input distance pi. This is the classical parity obstruction, with no novelty claim.

A stronger self-contained theorem also disproves the reverse bound for smooth, strictly positive, even densities with fixed upper and lower bounds, for every ambient n>=3 and fixed finite p>=1. The explicit harmonic family's input/output ratio is bounded below by a positive constant times k^((n-2)/(2p)). On even measures of the circle the transform is an isometry. No even-density W_infinity, optimal-modulus, restricted-support, or derivative-bounded-class result is claimed.

## Complete source and proof audit
The official Stephens contribution in OWR31/2008, printed pp.1762–1764, matches the transform and reverse question. The full fresh independent adversarial AI audit passed without corrections and was read and accepted by the parent publication review. This is AI-assisted, unrefereed work, not human or journal peer review.
